original_title: Kitab al-Filaha (Book of Agriculture)
author: Ibn al-Awwam (Abu Zakariya Yahya ibn Muhammad)
relevant_content: Practical agronomic manual; discusses rice (al-aruzz) cultivation under irrigation in Andalusi conditions; NOT translated into Latin or any vernacular during the Middle Ages — knowledge barrier documented
identifier: Filāḥa Texts Project, filaha.org/author_ibn_al_awwam.html; REMMM 123 'Studies on the agronomy of Al-Andalus' (2009)

original_title: La riziculture en al-Andalus (VIIIe-XVe siècles)
author: Lucie Bolens
relevant_content: Synthesis of Arabo-Muslim written testimony: ecological conditions of rice introduction, irrigation systems, techniques, consumption; rice a luxury food for privileged social groups in al-Andalus
evidence_category: Secondary synthesis of Arabic primary sources

original_title: From the Yangtze basin to the marshes of the Guadalquivir: introduction of Asian rice to Al-Andalus
author: J. Bravo Martínez (coord. A. Tena)
relevant_content: Rice reached the eastern Mediterranean by 2nd c. AD via Egypt/Palestine; Arabs diffused cultivation and consumption across North Africa and Iberia 9th-12th c.; in al-Andalus rice remained a luxury food

original_title: Between Archaeology and Text: Origins of Rice Consumption and Cultivation in the Middle East and the Mediterranean
author: Sureshkumar Muthukumaran
relevant_content: Archaeobotanical record: 196 charred rice grains at Roman military hospital, Novaesium/Neuss (1st quarter 1st c. AD; Knörzer 1966/1970); single grain in sacrificial pit, temple of Isis & Magna Mater, Mogontiacum/Mainz (late 1st c. AD; Zach 2002); grains at Tenedo/Zurzach (Nesbitt et al. 2010); all imports — rice not suited for growth in northern Europe
identifier: UCL Discovery eprint 1465980; PDF archived with SHA256

original_title: Plants from distant places: the 1st millennium CE archaeobotanical record from Iberia
author: Peña-Chocarro, L. et al.
relevant_content: Oryza sativa appears in the Iberian archaeobotanical record for the first time in the 1st millennium CE, together with rye, pearl millet, peach, mulberry, apricot, quince, medlar, citrus — i.e. rice enters as part of the Islamic-period crop package

original_title: Vella forgeries (false Arabic rescripts on Arab Sicily)
author: Giuseppe Vella (Franciscan friar
relevant_content: Exposed as forgery by 19th-c. scholarship (Amari-era Arabists)
evidence_category: Fabricated 9th-century rescript claiming rice was already cultivated/taxed in Sicily before AD 1000 under Arab rule; unmasked as forgery. Partly true only in that Arabs brought rice as a commodity (spice), never cultivated it in Sicily
column12: risoitaliano.eu/un-frate-burlone/ (2014); corroborated by Geotema 20-15 (2024), PDF archived

original_title: Note per uno studio sulla coltivazione del riso nella Sicilia sud orientale nei secoli XVII-XIX
author: AA.VV. (Geotema)
relevant_content: Sicilian rice cultivation documented only from 16th-17th c.; 12th-c. Ugo Falcando's 'De rebus gestis in Siciliae Regno' describes Palermo's gardens (oranges, sugar cane, melons) WITHOUT mentioning rice; literary references to Sicilian rice scant — marginal crop
identifier: Geotema 20-15 (2024); ageiweb.it PDF archived with SHA256

original_title: Galeazzo Maria Sforza letter to Niccolò de Roberti, 27 September 1475
author: Galeazzo Maria Sforza
relevant_content: Published/documented; discussed in Crawford & Alkala (2010) and Fondazione Estense journal
evidence_category: 12 sacks of rice sent as gift to Ercole I d'Este for sowing in the Ferrarese; Sforza already experimenting at Vigevano estate from ca. 1470-1472; at that time export of rice seed from Milan was prohibited by ducal order (export ban — monopoly protection, waived for this gift)

original_title: Furs de Valencia + Cartas puebla (James I of Aragon)
author: James I of Aragon (royal chancery)
modern_edition_or_translation: Published diplomatic collections; analyzed in HistAgrar 2021 and Universidad de Alicante study (2002)
relevant_content: Royal legal code and settlement charters PRESERVED Andalusi irrigation water rights: 'Et explectent aquas suas sicut est consuetum tempore Sarracenorum' (Sierra de Eslida carta puebla); Furs regulate cequiero/sobreacequiero offices; irrigated surface EXPANDED post-1238 under reparto de tierras
evidence_category: Primary documentary evidence — state protection of irrigation agriculture

original_title: Der Reishandel im Hanseraum (The rice trade in the Hanseatic Area)
author: Sabine Karg, Carsten Jahnke
relevant_content: From the cusp of the 14th century rice became increasingly important in Hanseatic trade; luxury good prized as thickener for almond-puddings and Lenten fare; all Hanseatic merchants acquainted with it; origins, routes, quantities and prices documented

original_title: Winchester Yields: A Study in Medieval Agricultural Productivity
author: J.Z. Titow
relevant_content: n/a
evidence_category: Primary quantitative dataset: gross yields per seed and per acre for wheat, barley, oats, mancorn/rye/drage on Winchester bishopric manors 1209-1349; sowing rates; highest/lowest manorial averages
column12: Cambridge University Press, ISBN 9780521083492; sample PDF archived

original_title: Yield ratios, 810-1820 (De oogstopbrengsten)
author: B.H. Slicher van Bath
relevant_content: Canonical compilation of seed-to-harvest yield ratios for cereals 810-1820 across Europe; baseline for medieval productivity comparison

original_title: Health, wellness and the allure of spices in the Middle Ages
author: Paul Freedman
relevant_content: Imported aromatic products (incl. rice-adjacent exotics) credited with preventive/curative properties; spices functioned as prestige elite goods AD 1200-1500 — frames K1 rice-as-import knowledge

original_title: The Causes of Slavery or Serfdom: A Hypothesis
author: Evsey Domar
relevant_content: Hypothesis: serfdom/slavery arises when land abundant + labor scarce + non-working owner class exists; landowners extract rent from labor not land — baseline theory for landlord-coercion mechanism analysis
identifier: J Economic History 30(1):18-32; DOI 10.1017/S0022050700078566; PDF archived

original_title: Tacuinum Sanitatis manuscripts (from Ibn Butlan, Taqwim al-Sihha, d. 1063)
author: Ibn Butlan / Latin redactors
date: 11th c. Arabic; 14th c. Latin illustrated copies
relevant_content: Rice (oriza) depicted/described among foodstuffs with medicinal properties — K1/K2 knowledge circulating in elite Latin-European milieux by late 14th c.

original_title: Phenological responses of upland rice along an altitudinal gradient (Madagascar field trials)
author: Raboin et al.
relevant_content: 10 upland O. sativa genotypes at 3 altitudes: at high altitude (Tmin 13°C / Tmax 19°C) grain yield strongly depressed, spikelet sterility driven by low temperature (genotype explains 68% of sterility variance) — modern bounded feasibility constraint on medieval upland rice in N. Europe
identifier: Environ. Exp. Bot. 94; DOI 10.1016/j.envexpbot.2012.12.007; PDF archived

original_title: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) — crop climate requirement compendium
author: TN Agriculture (crop improvement guide)
relevant_content: Rice: minimum temperatures for germination 10°C, flowering 23°C, grain formation 20°C; optimum growth 21-36°C, flowering 25-29°C; short-day plant; rainfall 1000-4500mm — used ONLY as bounded-feasibility constraint, not as medieval yield evidence

original_title: Yield Stability and GxE Interactions of Upland Rice (Madagascar Tropentag paper)
author: Raboin et al.
relevant_content: Upland rice trials: HA site Tmin 13°C/Tmax 19°C — yield depressed; consistent with S16

original_title: Islamic traditions of agroecology: cross-cultural experience, ideas and innovations
author: Karl Butzer
relevant_content: Islamic agronomy drew on Greek/eastern Mediterranean sphere; Andalusi hydraulic agriculture transferred institutional + technical package to Iberia
identifier: Butzer 1994, UT Austin author copy, PDF archived

original_title: Forme of Cury (Ryse/Rys recipes); Ménagier de Paris (blanc-manger)
author: Anon. (Richard II household) / Bourgeois de Paris
relevant_content: Rice appears as imported ingredient in elite late-medieval cookery north of the Alps — K1 commodity knowledge, NOT cultivation knowledge
identifier: standard scholarly editions; cross-checked via secondary literature

original_title: Régimen jurídico de las zonas húmedas del Reino de Valencia (XV-XVIII)
author: AA.VV. (Anuario de Historia del Derecho Español)
relevant_content: Medieval monarchs promoted drainage/sanitation of wetlands; transit restrictions through wetlands and pecuniary penalties; hygienic tutelage extended to rice plantations — arrozales treated as infectious-focus public-health danger from stagnant water + heat/humidity
evidence_category: Documented sanitary restriction of rice cultivation (motivated by fever outbreaks)

original_title: Food and Meaning: Christian Understandings of Muslim Food and Food Ways in Spain, 1250-1550
author: Olivia Remie Constable
relevant_content: Enrique IV of Castile criticized for eating Muslim foods seated on the ground in Muslim manner; Christian rhetoric progressively coded Muslim-associated foods as identity markers (impurity rhetoric) — rice perceived in post-conquest Valencia as 'Muslim food'

original_title: The Rhetoric of Impurity in Medieval Iberia
author: AA.VV.
relevant_content: 13th c. onward: rules prohibiting commensality; Christians condemned foods of 'circumstantial impurity' (contaminated by proximity to undesirable element); by early 15th c. Castilian law forbade Muslims selling edibles to Christians

original_title: Polémica higiénico-sanitaria por la ricicultura en los límites de la Albufera de Valencia (siglos XVIII-XIX)
author: AA.VV. (Univ. Alicante)
relevant_content: Albufera rice cultivation polemic 'desde tiempos inmemoriales': detractors invoking public health vs defenders economic; broad legislative control; prohibitions in multiple towns amid 'fiebres tercianas' outbreaks — culmination of medieval sanitary regime
evidence_category: Post-period legislative record of sanitary rice restriction

original_title: History of Spain's Relationship with Rice / DO Arroz de Valencia (Santos Ruiz) via Las Provincias 2015
author: Santos Ruiz (DO Arroz de Valencia) / press synthesis
relevant_content: Post-1238 conquest: rice perceived as Muslim food occupying land for 'traditionally Christian products'; from 14th c. medical theory linked wetland rice zones to fevers; intermittent growing prohibitions 15th-18th c., especially post-1609 Morisco expulsion; earliest limitation attempts dated to 1238 conquest aftermath
evidence_category: Secondary/press — medieval sanitary limitation + confessional stigma

original_title: Lake Effects: Transnational History and the Making of a Valencian Landscape
author: AA.VV. (dissertation
relevant_content: n/a
evidence_category: Fears of malaria led Spain's rulers to outlaw rice cultivation in Albufera marshlands for several centuries
